reactions.name: Haber Process
reactions.context: Industrial synthesis of ammonia for fertilizer. High pressure, moderate temperature (450°C) optimizes yield vs reaction rate.

le_chatelier_notes.increase_pressure: More moles on reactant side (4 vs 2) → equilibrium shifts RIGHT, more NH₃.
le_chatelier_notes.decrease_temperature: Shifts RIGHT, more NH₃ (but slower reaction rate — hence catalysts).

reactions.name: CO₂ Dissolution
reactions.context: Ocean acidification. More CO₂ in the atmosphere → shifts RIGHT → more H⁺ → oceans become acidic → coral reefs dissolve.

le_chatelier_notes.add_CO2: Shifts RIGHT, ocean becomes more acidic.
le_chatelier_notes.remove_CO2: Shifts LEFT, ocean becomes more basic.
le_chatelier_notes.increase_temperature: Shifts LEFT, less dissolution (hot water holds less CO₂).
le_chatelier_notes.add_H+: Shifts LEFT, removing carbonate ions — damages shells.

reactions.name: Iron Thiocyanate
reactions.context: Classic demo: colorless solutions turn blood-red. Adding Fe³⁺ intensifies color; adding Na⁺ dilutes it. Used to study Le Chatelier's Principle visually.

le_chatelier_notes.add_NaF: F⁻ binds Fe³⁺ → removes reactant → shifts LEFT, color fades.
le_chatelier_notes.dilute: Both concentrations decrease — net shift LEFT by reaction quotient.

reactions.name: Dinitrogen Tetroxide
reactions.context: Brown NO₂ (dioxide) converts to colorless N₂O₄ (dimer) in the cold. Put the flask in ice → it turns pale. Warm it → turns brown again.

le_chatelier_notes.increase_temperature: Endothermic in reverse → shifts LEFT, more brown NO₂.
le_chatelier_notes.increase_pressure: 2 moles → 1 mole, shifts RIGHT, more N₂O₄.

reactions.name: HCl Synthesis
reactions.context: Extremely favorable — Keq ≈ 10³¹. Essentially goes to completion. Shows that very large Keq means the reaction heavily favors products.

le_chatelier_notes.increase_pressure: Equal moles on both sides (2 vs 2), no net shift.
le_chatelier_notes.increase_temperature: Exothermic → shifts LEFT, but Keq is so large it barely matters.
